articles.title: Dark personality traits predict support for violence by both Israel and Hamas
articles.summary: A new study indicates that psychopathy and sadism predict support for violence on both sides of the Israel-Hamas conflict. While ideology usually drives partisan loyalty, these dark personality traits are linked to a broader acceptance of violence.

articles.title: High intelligence may exacerbate impulsivity in children with ADHD
articles.summary: A large study reveals that while high intelligence in children with ADHD is associated with better focus, it is also linked to greater impulsivity, challenging the idea that a high IQ always protects against severe symptoms.

articles.title: “Mankeeping” takes a toll on women’s mental health and relationship satisfaction, study suggests
articles.summary: A newly developed psychological survey measures "mankeeping"—the unpaid labor women perform to manage their male partners' social lives. Findings show that this effort is strongly associated with relationship burnout, lower satisfaction, and psychological distress.

articles.title: Scientists restore a brain protein and reverse signs of aging in mice
articles.summary: Scientists found that declining levels of the brain protein Menin may help drive aging, with lower levels in mice linked to inflammation, cognitive decline, weaker bones, and thinner skin. Restoring Menin reversed several age-related changes, while the amino acid D-serine improved cognition, hinting at a potentially intriguing new target for healthy aging.

articles.title: These blood thinners may have an unexpected benefit for Alzheimer’s patients
articles.summary: Newer blood thinners may do more than prevent strokes in people with Alzheimer’s disease and atrial fibrillation. Researchers found that patients taking NOACs experienced a slower decline in cognitive function than those using warfarin or no blood thinners. The effect was modest each year but could add up over time.

articles.summary: Researchers recently investigated the pathways connecting caffeine use disorder, depression, and sleep quality. Their findings illustrate how problematic caffeine consumption and specific use motives correlate with impaired sleep and mental health outcomes.

articles.title: Textbooks may have misdrawn this basic brain structure for 100 years
articles.summary: Scientists discovered that brain-cell axons may not be smooth tubes as textbooks have shown for more than a century, but instead naturally resemble strings of tiny pearls. Those pearl-like structures can change with neural activity and may help control how quickly electrical signals travel through the brain.

articles.title: Hidden “immune organ” in the skull may help fight brain cancer
articles.summary: Scientists discovered a hidden “immune organ” inside the skull that acts as a rapid first responder against brain cancer in mice. Strengthening this local immune defense improved tumor rejection and survival, raising the possibility of new treatments that target the skull directly.

articles.title: Scientists recreated what mice saw from brain activity alone
articles.summary: Scientists reconstructed videos from the brain activity of mice, producing 10-second clips based only on signals from neurons in the visual cortex. The breakthrough could help reveal how the brain reshapes what we see before it becomes our perception of reality.

articles.title: Everyday physical activity is linked to a major boost in energy and mood
articles.summary: By analyzing nearly a million hours of movement data, researchers found that everyday activities like walking and chores frequently coincide with higher energy levels, highlighting a deep, bidirectional link between physical activity and emotional well-being.

articles.title: Brain waves predict sexual side effects of common depression medications
articles.summary: A quick brain wave test may soon help doctors predict if a patient will experience sexual side effects from antidepressants. Measuring serotonin activity before treatment could guide medication choices and improve the quality of life for patients with depression.

articles.title: Regularized Emphatic Temporal-Difference Learning: Stability under Constant Stepsizes
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.19170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emphatic temporal-difference learning (ETD) stabilizes the expected off-policy TD update and changes its projection geometry, but neither property determines constant-stepsize sampled dynamics. We construct an ergodic two-state counterexample in which the ETD mean map contracts while the sampled product has a positive top Lyapunov exponent. Regenerative-cycle analysis separates this sign from the infinite variance of the follow-on trace. We introduce regularized emphatic TD (RETD), a normalized first-order post-shock repair that leaves the trace

articles.title: BioPhys-Bridge: A Benchmark for Interdisciplinary Scientific Reasoning in Physics-Grounded Biological Research
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.19180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models face unique challenges in analyzing interdisciplinary scientific research literature. In biophysics research, faithful answers require grounding observed data in source evidence, interpreting it through a quantitative physics model, and linking it to a biological mechanism. To address this challenge, we introduce BioPhys-Bridge, a novel benchmark dataset for evidence-grounded scientific reasoning over biophysical literature. Each case contains evidence blocks, stable evidence IDs, quantitative values, units, equations, assumptions

articles.title: What Do We Expect from LLMs? Mapping the Design of LLM Benchmarks
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.19182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarks are central to how progress in large language models (LLMs) is assessed and communicated. Yet model rankings alone reveal little about how evaluation requirements themselves are changing. The expanding variety of benchmarks offers another perspective: what researchers expect LLMs to do, and what they count as successful performance. articles.title: Position: It is Time to Virtualize Foundation Models with a Self-evolving Operating System Layer
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.19203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI applications have shifted from single, monolithic foundation models (FM) to compound agentic systems. Yet today's stacks remain fragmented: even as protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) ease tool/agent connectivity, each framework embeds an implicit runtime for state, memory, budgets, and guardrails, making behavior non-portable and governance brittle. articles.title: Generative Query Suggestion via Intent Coverage and Query-Level Credit Assignment
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.19209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative query suggestion aims to enhance user engagement by anticipating user intents and recommending relevant follow-up queries. A central challenge is to generate slates whose individual queries are useful while the slate covers distinct intents. We propose an Intent-Driven Query Suggestion Framework with dual-stage optimization. First, intent-aware diversity modeling constructs intent-aligned supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data and uses an Intent-Aware Diversity Reward to optimize intent coverage. Second, query-level credit assignment routes

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.19213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce layer-wise curriculum learning for efficient LLM compression.
